title: Stewardship framework for customer pricing requests and marketplace cost attribution
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We receive a high volume of non-bug customer requests related to pricing, commitment offers, invoice handling and marketplace crediting. Without a concise stewardship model and attribution rules, teams (Sales, Finance, PMs) take ad-hoc approaches that increase cycle time, risk misbilling, and create inconsistent customer experiences.

Goal: Create a lightweight, operational stewardship framework and decision lattice that (1) captures essential request metadata at intake, (2) assigns ownership and SLA lane, (3) scores and prioritizes requests against quantifiable business heuristics (revenue, legal risk, operational cost, strategic account), and (4) standardizes marketplace cost attribution and invoice mapping rules. Deliverables: intake form template, triage rubric, mapping table for commitment types -> invoice/ledger lines, and an owner/resolution playbook.
acceptance_criteria: A single intake form is published and used by Sales/CS for all pricing/commitment/invoice requests
Requests are automatically assigned to a steward within 4 business hours using the new routing rules
Priority scoring produces an actionable rank for the backlog (P0/P1/P2 lanes) with reproducible rationale
Marketplace credit attribution matrix is reviewed by Finance and results in a one-page mapping table used by Billing engineers
Pilot with three active enterprise customers completes and we capture feedback (time-to-resolution, accuracy, CSAT)
decision_log: 2025-01-21: Chosen scoring axes: Revenue Delta (ARR/one-time), Legal/Compliance Risk, Operational Complexity (engineering hours), Strategic Weight (customer tier). Each axis normalized 0-10.
2025-01-28: Adopted 'steward' role per request that can be PM, Finance Lead, or Sales Lead depending on the request type; steward is responsible for final approval and invoicing mapping.

2025-02-03: Marketplace credit attribution will be anchored to SKU-level tags and a simple three-tier rule (Marketplace fee absorb, Marketplace credit, Customer-borne). Finance to validate edge cases.
2025-02-05: Decided to keep the intake form minimal (12 fields) to encourage adoption; additional artifacts collected on a follow-up cadence.
stakeholders: Billing Platform Team - Engineering (billing mapping implementation)
required_artifacts: Commitment -> Invoice mapping spreadsheet (Google Sheets) - link TBD
Sample customer requests (redacted) - for scoring calibration
Playbook doc: steward responsibilities + SLA matrix - Confluence
out_of_scope: Changing existing product pricing models for self-serve customers
Deep rework of Marketplace billing engine (this ticket focuses on mapping and rules only)
Resolving historical invoice disputes older than 12 months (handled by Finance separately)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Finance disagrees with three-tier attribution rules -> Mitigation: schedule a joint review session and add exception handling column in mapping table
Risk: Sales bypasses intake to fast-track high-touch deals -> Mitigation: make intake a mandatory step for any pricing commitment > $50k and add enforcement via CRM hook
Risk: Overly complex rubric reduces triage speed -> Mitigation: pilot a simplified 4-axis model and iterate after two-week pilot
implementation_notes: Step 1: Publish intake form and embed in Sales playbook (owner: Sofia)
Step 2: Build routing rules in Linear/ops-scripts that assign steward based on request_type + customer_tier (owner: Liam)
Step 3: Finance to review and sign off on mapping spreadsheet; build test cases for common SKUs (owner: Rohit)
Step 4: Run 2-week pilot with three enterprise accounts and capture metrics: time-to-first-response, time-to-resolution, billing accuracy rate, CSAT (owner: Ava)
Step 5: Iterate on rubric thresholds and publish final playbook; hand off to Program Ops for steady-state operations
